record.context_brief: shear versus bulk tradeoff with voids
record.original_question: For an isotropic composite made from one elastic phase and void, let kappa* and mu* denote the effective bulk and shear moduli and let kappa and mu be the moduli of the solid phase. The elementary bounds imply mu* - c kappa* <= mu for every c>0. Can this inequality be sharpened in two and/or three dimensions for some range of c>0, or equivalently can one construct composites whose effective moduli approach the limiting pair (kappa*,mu*)=(0,mu)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9: The bounds (4.1) imply µ∗ − cκ∗ ≤ µ for all c > 0. Can this inequality be improved, in 2 and/or 3 dimensions, for a range of c > 0? Alternatively, can one construct composites of an elastic phase with void with (κ∗, µ∗) arbitrarily close to (0, µ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an isotropic two-phase composite in dimension d ∈ {2,3} obtained by mixing one linearly elastic isotropic solid phase, with bulk modulus κ > 0 and shear modulus μ > 0, with void (the second "phase" is empty space, having zero moduli). Let κ* and μ* denote the effective bulk and shear moduli of the resulting macroscopically isotropic composite, taken over all admissible microgeometries and all volume fractions of the solid phase.

The elementary (Hashin–Shtrikman type / Voigt) bounds imply that
   μ* − c·κ* ≤ μ
for every constant c > 0.

(a) Determine whether this inequality can be strictly sharpened — i.e., replaced by μ* − c·κ* ≤ μ − δ(c) with some δ(c) > 0 — for some range of c > 0, in dimension d = 2 and/or d = 3.

(b) Equivalently, decide whether there exist sequences of admissible isotropic composites of the solid phase with void whose effective moduli (κ*, μ*) approach the limiting pair (0, μ); that is, whether the point (κ*, μ*) = (0, μ) lies in the closure of the set of attainable effective moduli pairs.
artifact.category_tag: bounds on effective moduli of composites
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any publication explicitly resolving this question about whether the effective-moduli pair (κ*, μ*) = (0, μ) is attainable in the closure for isotropic elastic-phase/void composites in 2D or 3D, nor a sharpening of the bound μ* − cκ* ≤ μ. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the available literature, but no definitive evidence of resolution or non-resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: The Theory of Composites — Graeme W. Milton
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatise on bounds for effective moduli of composites; the question of attainability of extreme (κ*, μ*) pairs for elastic/void mixtures is discussed but not fully resolved in 2D/3D.
status_evidence.claim: The standard reference does not record a resolution of whether (0, μ) is in the closure of attainable (κ*, μ*).

status_evidence.title: Bounds on the Effective Moduli of Composite Materials — Gibiansky
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known bounds; sharp bounds in the elastic/void limit for the diagonal μ* − cκ* are not established for all c.
status_evidence.claim: No improvement of μ* − cκ* ≤ μ is recorded in this survey.
